Turnover of features between consecutive samples

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/getTurnover.R
getTurnover.Rd

Calculates the proportion of features that appear or disappear between each sample and the previous sample of the same subject.

getTurnover(x, ...)

addTurnover(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
getTurnover(
  x,
  time.col,
  assay.type = "counts",
  time.interval = 1L,
  time.lag = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  method = c("total", "appearance", "disappearance"),
  detection = 0,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
addTurnover(x, name = c("turnover", "time_diff", "ref_samples"), ...)

Arguments

x

A SummarizedExperiment object.

...

additional arguments.

time.col

Character scalar. Specifies a name of the column from colData that identifies the sampling time points for the samples.

assay.type

Character scalar. Specifies which assay values are used in the dissimilarity estimation. (Default: "counts")

time.interval

Integer scalar. Indicates the increment between time steps. By default, the function compares each sample to the previous one. If you need to take every second, every third, or so, time step, then increase this accordingly. (Default: 1L)

time.lag

NULL or Numeric scalar. If specified, each sample is compared to the earlier sample whose time is closest to time.lag time units before it, instead of counting time steps with time.interval. Useful when samples are not evenly spaced in time. The first sample of each group gets NA. (Default: NULL)

group

Character scalar. Specifies a name of the column from colData that identifies the grouping of the samples. (Default: NULL)

method

Character scalar. The turnover to calculate: "total", "appearance" or "disappearance". (Default: "total")

detection

Numeric scalar. Abundance above which a feature is considered present. (Default: 0)

name

Character vector. Specifies the names of the three columns of results. (Default: c("turnover", "time_diff", "ref_samples"))

Value

getTurnover returns a DataFrame with one row per sample and the turnover, the time from the previous sample and the previous sample. addTurnover adds these to colData(x). The first sample of each subject gets NA.

Details

Turnover (Hallett et al. 2016) compares which features are present (above detection) in two samples. With \(G\) features gained, \(L\) features lost and \(N\) features present in either sample, total turnover is \((G + L) / N\), appearance is \(G / N\) and disappearance is \(L / N\). The previous sample is chosen as in getStepwiseDivergence().

References

Hallett LM, et al. (2016) codyn: An R package of community dynamics metrics. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 7(10), 1146-1151. doi: 10.1111/2041-210X.12569

See also

getStepwiseDivergence()

Examples

library(miaTime)

# Two faecal samples of each subject in an IBD cohort
data(HMP_2019_ibdmdb)
tse <- HMP_2019_ibdmdb

# Proportion of taxa gained since the first sample
tse <- addTurnover(tse, time.col = "days_from_first_collection",
    group = "subject_id", assay.type = "relabundance",
    method = "appearance", name = c("gained", "time_diff", "ref_samples"))

# Proportion of taxa lost
tse[["lost"]] <- getTurnover(tse, time.col = "days_from_first_collection",
    group = "subject_id", assay.type = "relabundance",
    method = "disappearance")[["turnover"]]

df <- as.data.frame(colData(tse))
df <- df[!is.na(df[["gained"]]), ]
head(df[, c("subject_id", "disease_subtype", "time_diff", "gained", "lost")])
#>          subject_id disease_subtype time_diff     gained       lost

#> CSM79HLM      C3003              UC       251 0.17910448 0.16417910
#> CSM7KOJG      C3009              CD       238 0.24752475 0.49504950
#> CSM7KOSV      C3021              CD       215 0.02666667 0.33333333
